p:cNvPr.descr: An image showing the formation of a sugar nucleotide. At the top is sugar phosphate, which begins with sugar biding right to O (red), which binds right to P (red). P binds right O- (red), down to O- (red), and double binds up to O (red). A plus sign is to the right of O- (red) to add NTP, which begins with O-, which binds right P, which binds down to O-, and double binds up to O. P also binds right to O, which binds right to P. That P binds down to O- and double binds up to O. P also binds right to O, which binds right to P. P double binds up to O, binds down to O- and binds right to O, which binds right to ribose, which binds to base. This top diagram has a red curved arrow going over the top from the last red O- pointing to the last P. There is a very small red arrow pointing from the last P to the O to the left of it. Below sugar phosphate is a single black arrow that has two arrows darting from it pointing to the pyrophosphate (PP) diagram and the sugar nucleotide (NDP-sugar) diagram. To the left of those arrows is NDP-sugar pyrophosphorylase (in blue). The pyrophosphate (PP) diagram on the left begins with -O, which binds right to P. P double binds up to O, binds down to O-, and binds right to O, which binds right to P. P double binds up to O, and binds down to O- and binds right to O-. The sugar nucelotide diagram to the right of the pyrophosphate diagram begins with sugar, which binds right O (red), which binds right to P (red). P binds down to O- (red) and double binds up to O (red). It also binds right to O (red), which binds right to P. P double binds up to O, binds down to O- and right to O. I binds to ribose, which binds to base. Below the pyrophosphaste diagram is a black arrow pointing to the phosphate (P1) diagram. In the middle of the arrow pointing down is inorganic pyrophosphatase (in blue). There is a 2 left of the diagram. P binds left to -O, down to O-, and right to OH. It also double binds up to O. At the bottom of all diagrams, it says, "Net reaction: Sugar phosphate + NTP [arrow to the right] NDP-sugar + 2P.

p:cNvPr.descr: An image showing the chain of UDP-glucose (a sugar nucleotide). On the top left is the D-Glucosyl group in a red box. It is a hexagon with thick black lines at the bottom three sides. Clockwise from the first point on the left: H binds down to HO; CH2OH binds down to H (inside hexagon); O is the third point; H binds down to O; H (inside hexagon) binds down to HO; and HO (inside hexagon) binds down to H. The O on the fourth point binds down to P (all not in red box), which binds left to -O, double binds down to O, and binds right to O, which binds right to P. P double binds up to O, binds right to O- and down to O, which binds right to CH2 (in new red box identified as iridine). CH2 binds down to H on the first point of a pentagon. Clockwise: O is the second point; N binds down to H; H (inside pentagon) binds down to OH; and H (inside pentagon) binds down to OH. The N on the third point binds up and left, then double binds down and left to O., which binds up to HN, which binds up and right, then double binds up to O. O then binds down and right, then double binds down, then binds left and down back to N.
